# Register of commitments

This register lists everything the theory assumes, defines, or leaves open, one entry per item.
Each later paper adds its own entries in a new layer and cites the register for what it builds on.
A result in any layer should be traceable, through the **Requires** fields, to the entries it rests on.

The register is generated from the entries in `organon/graph/mec/` (one file per entry) and
`organon/method/`; the entry with id X is in the file `X.md` there.

**Entry kinds.**
*Premise*: the starting point that motivates the commitments.
*Commitment*: admitted, not derived; each must be argued for where it is introduced.
*Definition*: introduces a term in terms of existing entries; adds nothing new.
*Convention*: a feature of the presentation, not a claim about what is described.
*Exclusion*: a view the commitments rule out as a precondition of registration.
*Presupposition*: assumed by the text without being stated as a commitment; to be examined.
*Open*: a question the layer raises and does not answer.
*Consequence*: follows from the entries it requires; recorded so that it can be cited, adds nothing new.
*Branch*: a further analysis compatible with every entry it builds on; kept open, not adopted.
*Closed*: an analysis that contradicts an entry; recorded with the entry it contradicts.
*Decision*: a choice between readings, with its reasons and whether it rests on a claim or on method.
*Objection*: an attack on an entry, with its current status.
*Friction*: anything that blocks progress or prompts revision, with its kind, the entries between
which it arises, and how it was resolved, if it was (see `organon/method/schema.md`).

Section numbers refer to *A Minimal Epistemic Core* (`latex/epistemic_core.tex`).

---

## Method (all layers)

The method is itself a set of assumptions. It is recorded here so that it can be examined and
revised like any other entry, and so that a result can be checked for features that come from the
method rather than from what it describes. It applies to every investigation in the repository;
test protocols are in `organon/method/`.

### Rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| M1 | Every result states whether it requires only the trunk (the entries that every analysis must satisfy) or a named branch. |
| M2 | A branch is closed when it contradicts an entry of the trunk, or can be kept only by readmitting an exclusion. Closing a branch does not affect results that do not require it. |
| M3 | Branches are not exclusive. They may be combined where they are consistent; some concern only one kind of domain. |
| M4 | When a branch is closed, record whether it was closed by a commitment about what is described or by a methodological presupposition (Mp-). A branch closed only by method is reopened if that presupposition is revised. |
| M5 | From time to time, rebuild a step under a different method (for instance, richer instead of minimal, or coherentist instead of foundational) and record which results survive. A result that survives several methods is less likely to be a feature of the method. |
| M6 | A notion may be left primitive when four conditions hold: any definition of it would use it, or something no clearer, or would readmit what the theory excludes; its use is bound by stated conditions, so that a misuse can be shown; it has instances in more than one domain; and the theory says what work it does. |

### Methodological presuppositions

| Id | Presupposition | What it may cost |
|---|---|---|
| Mp-parsimony | Fewer commitments are preferred to more. This is a value of the method, not a claim about what is described. It contributed to the choice of Reading A. | Truths that require richer structure may be excluded for economy alone. |
| Mp-classical | Branches are closed by contradiction under classical logic. | A domain in which some contradictions hold would be closed off by the method. A branch that is consistent but false is never closed. |
| Mp-foundational | The theory is built upward from a trunk, each layer resting on those below. The alternative, that commitments support one another without a bottom layer (coherentism), has not been argued against. | Commitments of a lower layer cannot be revised in the light of a higher one without restructuring the register. |
| Mp-separable | Frame and content differ by role, not by kind. At any moment some entries function as frame (they are held fixed while others are examined) and others as content; the same entry can play either role, and content can force a change in what is held fixed. Each opener records what it holds fixed in `holds_fixed`. | No entry is protected by being method. A rule or presupposition can be refuted by what an investigation finds, and closures that rested on it (M4) must then be reopened. Conversely, nothing is examined without something else held fixed for the moment. |
| Mp-schema | The entry types, statuses, fields and link types of organon, as defined in method/schema.md and enforced by tools/check.py. Recorded as an entry so that frictions and revisions can name it. | Every fixed vocabulary is a set of differences supplied by the apparatus, not by what is recorded. Where a case does not fit, the vocabulary must be changed rather than the case forced. |

## Layer 1: the minimal epistemic core

### Question

| Id | Question | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Q0** | What preconditions enable knowledge, of any kind, prior to knowledge itself? | The author's formulation when the work began: "a minimal epistemological core is proposed (what preconditions enable knowledge, prior to knowledge itself)". The core claims necessary conditions only, not sufficient ones. |

### Premise

| Id | Statement | Notes | § |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pr-det** | Whatever is some way in particular differs: there is a way that it is not, and its being this way in particular, as against any other, lies in that. This does not reduce what a thing is to how it differs: whether a thing's character consists in its differences, or is more than them, is left open. Applied without exception: to what a relation is of, to the registering, and to the conditions of whatever receives. | Asserted, not derived: it is what the account takes "in particular" to mean. Its ground: a way that excluded nothing would mark nothing, and a thing that was no way in particular could not be what anything is of. It leaves open whether the other term is actual; that is settled by Pr-rec. Point of refusal: holding that a thing may be some way in particular while differing from nothing, actual or not, in that respect. | 2 |
| **Pr-rec** | The relation under study is the one in which something is taken up, and what is taken up is that to which the taking-up is due: a registering holds, at least partly, in virtue of what it registers. | It marks out which relation is analysed; it is not a hypothesis that cases might overturn. Its content is shown by what falls short of it. Likeness, correspondence and ordering hold between two contrasts by how each is; if they sufficed, nothing would be received by anything. Agreement by arrangement owes whatever aboutness it has to a dependence somewhere in the case; with no dependence anywhere it is coincidence, which is of nothing in particular. Point of refusal: holding that an epistemic relation, in its basic form, need not be receptive, which the account regards as a change of subject. The word and the idea are the author's from the first draft ("receptive dependence", "reception requires a connection not supplied by either participant alone"). | 2 |
| **P** | In its basic form, an epistemic relation is a receptive relation to something in particular. (P1) What it is of is a difference: X as it differs, in some respect, from another actual term. (P2) That by which it is of that difference, the registering, is itself a difference, and it holds at least partly in virtue of the first. "Basic" means prior to concepts and descriptions. | Motivates D, R and C. The core claims necessity only: P yields necessary conditions, not sufficient ones. P does not cover aboutness by description, of the future, or of mathematical objects; whether these are built from basic aboutness is Q5. | 2 |

### Commitments

| Id | Statement | Requires | Does not establish | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C** | *Receptive dependence.* A contrast K′, borne by a field, holds at least partly in virtue of a contrast K borne by F. | Df-bears | Which way F is; understanding, representation, order, acquisition, retention. | 5 |
| **C-asym** | *Direction.* Nothing holds in virtue of itself. The dependence has a direction: that one contrast holds in virtue of another does not bring with it that the second holds in virtue of the first. Whether two distinct contrasts can each hold partly in virtue of the other is left open, and so is whether the dependence is transitive. The dependence holds between contrasts, not between fields: F and R may each depend on the other through different contrasts. | C, Df-roles |  | 5 |
| **C-actual** | *Actuality.* C relates two contrasts that both hold. It says nothing about what would hold otherwise. | C, Ps-actual |  | 5 |
| **C-partial** | *Partiality.* The registering contrast holds at least partly in virtue of the registered contrast. Whatever else it holds in virtue of may lie in the field that bears it. The core claims neither that there is always such a remainder nor any bound on it. | C |  | 5 |

### Conditions of method

Not claims of the core: rules about what the reconstruction articulates.

| Id | Condition | Requires | What it does not do | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D-scope** | *Scope of the reconstruction.* The reconstruction articulates only fields taken to bear the contrasts it specifies, and concerns only contrasts the account specifies. Specification chooses the respect and selects a contrast borne in it; that it does not create the contrast is a stipulation of the route, not a result. | Df-bears, Df-specified | It does not argue against the view that all differentiation is supplied. It states that view's cost: if it held, nothing would be registered in P's sense. | 3 |

### Consequences

| Id | Statement | Requires | Does not establish | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D** | *Borne contrast (formerly Differentiability).* Every field in which a registered articulation is realized bears that articulation's contrast. | Df-registration, Df-realized | Which contrasts a field bears, or of what form; that any field bears a contrast apart from registration; any modal claim about F. What the reconstruction may articulate is D-scope, a condition of method. | 4 |
| **R** | *The registering contrast and its bearer.* In an instance of C, the contrast K′ that depends is distinct from the registered contrast K, since by C-asym nothing holds in virtue of itself. What bears K′ is, insofar as it does, a field (Field-aspect); R names it. | C, C-asym, Field-aspect | A knowing subject. Whether R and F are distinct fields, parts of one field, or the same field bearing two contrasts. | 6 |
| **Lone** | *A lone term.* What differs from no actual other term in a given respect is a position in no contrast in that respect, and the core provides for registering nothing of it in that respect. | Df-bears, Df-registration | That there is any such thing. | 4 |

Argument for **P** (§2): P follows from two principles. By determinacy (Pr-det), what a relation is of is some way in particular, and so differs in some respect. By receptivity (Pr-rec), the registering is due to what it is of, and what something is due to must itself hold. For the registering to be a taking-up of the thing's being this way in particular, and not merely of something that happens to be some way, it must be due to what makes that way a particular one, which is its differing from another. So what is taken up is a difference between terms both actual (P1). The relation is of X as it differs; X need not be nothing but its differing, and the registering may be due to more of X than that difference, which is one reason the dependence is "at least partly". The registering is itself some way in particular, and it holds; so it differs from another actual condition, and the contrast between the two holds at least partly in virtue of the first difference, since what one of its positions is, is due to it (P2).

Argument for **Ps-actual, C-actual** (§2): What something is due to must itself hold; so what is taken up is a difference that holds, between terms both actual, and the same goes for the registering. Alternatives might enter in three places, and none is prior to registration. In what is taken up: an alternative cannot be that in virtue of which anything holds. In the dependence: dependence and what would have held otherwise come apart in both directions (K′ may be due to K although something else would have brought K′ about had K not held; and neither of two contrasts may hold without the other although both are due to a third), so what would have held otherwise is evidence of dependence, not what it consists in. In the receiver: a repertoire has to be held by actual conditions that stand for what is not the case, and such a receiver already registers and retains.

Argument for **D** (§4): Registration is always of a specified articulation realized in F (Df-registration). An articulation is realized in F when its specified terms pick out positions of a contrast F bears in its respect (Df-realized). So F bears that contrast.

Argument for **R** (§6): C relates two contrasts, and by C-asym no contrast holds in virtue of itself, so the contrast that depends is a second contrast. Whatever bears a contrast is, insofar as it does, a field (Field-aspect). The receiving field distinguishes nothing: the account picks out its contrast, as it picks out the target's.

Argument for **C** (§5): C states P2 exactly and adds no commitment to it. That F bears a contrast and that another field bears one leave the two contrasts unconnected; likeness, correspondence, ordering and agreement due to a third contrast are relations in which the one contributes nothing to the other.

### Definitions

| Id | Term | Definition | Requires | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Df-bears | bearing a contrast; position; specified term | "Field F bears a contrast in respect δ" is primitive. It is bound by four conditions: a contrast is always in some respect; it has two positions, and no position differs from itself; its positions are both actual; and it does not divide what bears it exhaustively. A contrast is always borne by something. A *position* is a place in a contrast a field bears. A *specified term* is what a description picks out; it may pick out nothing. By stipulation, two contrasts are the same when they have the same positions and the same respect. | none | 3, 4 |
| Df-field | field F | A field is whatever bears a contrast, insofar as it does: an aspect, not a kind of thing. F designates the field under consideration as target, which fixes the scope of the inquiry. Implies no region, objects, boundary, or presentation to a subject. | Df-bears | 3 |
| Df-articulation | articulation ⟨a,δ,b⟩_F | A particular differentiation of F; a, b are its *terms* and δ its *respect*. Its *contrast* is the difference of a and b in δ: two articulations may share a respect and have different contrasts. Terms are positions, not prior objects. | Df-bears | 4 |
| Df-realized | realized articulation | Its specified terms a and b pick out positions of a contrast F bears in δ (Df-bears). The direction of δ, if any, is stated in terms of the respect, not by the order of the terms. The terms are not alternatives. | Df-articulation, Df-bears | 4 |
| Df-specified | specified articulation | Its terms and respect are fixed, by the account, not by F. Specification selects without creating, and can fail. It is how an account states an instance; no registration depends on it. | Df-articulation | 4 |
| Df-conditions | conditions r, r′ of R | The positions of a contrast borne by R, written r and r′; both actual positions of one contrast, neither alternatives nor stages. Specified by the account, as for any field. Need not share the form of an articulation of F; no pairing with the terms of F is implied. | Df-bears | 6 |
| Df-matching | matching | The terms of an articulation are paired with distinct conditions of R (a with r, b with r′). Symmetric. | Df-articulation, Df-conditions | 5 |
| Df-roles | target, receiver | In an instance of C, the contrast depended upon is the *registered* contrast and the contrast that depends is the *registering* contrast. The field that bears the first is the *target* in that instance; the field that bears the second, the *receiver*. Roles belong to contrasts first and to fields through them; one field may be both, through different contrasts. Roles are positions in C, not natures of what occupies them. | C | 5 |
| Df-registration | registration | A contrast K borne by F is registered by a contrast K′ when C holds between them: K′ holds at least partly in virtue of K. The field R that bears K′ is then said to register K. Always registration *of* a particular contrast, never of F without qualification; an actual relation, not a disposition. A contrast registers every contrast it holds at least partly in virtue of (Dec-indiscriminate). | C | 7 |

### Conventions

| Id | Convention | § |
|---|---|---|
| Cv-two | A contrast is between two positions. An articulation is written with two terms for that reason; a differentiation among more terms is a number of contrasts. | 4 |
| Cv-letters | F and R are named for the positions they occupy in the instances considered; nothing in R or C uses the notion of a receiver. | 5 |
| Cv-arrow | If C is written as an arrow, the same symbol must not also denote order. | 9 |
| Cv-figures | In figures, terms are marks, never areas; F and R are column headings, never enclosures; one arrow style is reserved for C; grey marks what belongs only to the theorist's description. | 4, 5, 7 |

### Exclusions (as preconditions of registration)

| Id | Excluded view | Excluded by | § |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | The reconstruction concerns a respect whose holding depends, even partly, on the specification or its notation (order, labels and grouping of terms are examples), where the bearer of that respect is not the target; this includes respects relating target positions to notation positions. | D-scope, as a matter of scope, not as a result of the core. | 3 |
| E1-self | A receiver merely differing within itself, where its contrast does not hold even partly in virtue of the target's contrast, is registration. | C ("partly in virtue of"). A field may register one of its own contrasts, but only through a distinct contrast of its own: C-asym implies that nothing holds in virtue of itself. | 5 |
| E2 | Registration consists in resemblance or term-by-term correspondence. | C: a correspondence between terms, however exact, is symmetric and supplies no dependence. | 5 |
| E3 | Registration is a transfer from target to receiver. | Df-registration | 7 |
| E4 | A repertoire of alternatives, in F, in R, or elsewhere, is a precondition of registration. | Df-realized, Df-conditions | 4, 7 |
| E5 | Time, or order of any kind, is a precondition of registration. | Df-registration (defined without order) | 9 |
| E6 | A knowing subject, concepts, or representations precede registration. | D, R, C (none involves them) | 6, 7 |

None of these denies that the excluded structures occur in particular epistemic relations; wherever
they are needed, they must enter as further commitments.

### Presuppositions (used but not yet stated as commitments)

These are assumed by the text of Layer 1 and are to be examined, accepted as commitments, or removed.

| Id | Presupposition | Where it appears | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ps-modal | "Admits" expresses a capacity of F (and of R) itself, not a stock of possibilities held anywhere. | D, R; §3 | examined |
| Ps-actual | Contrasts hold between actual terms only. | Df-realized, Df-conditions | examined |
| Ps-relata | Terms are positions within an articulation; whether relations are prior to relata, or the theory is neutral, is not settled. | Df-articulation; §4 | examined |
| Ps-ground | "In virtue of" is an asymmetric dependence that relates what actually obtains and need not be counterfactual; it is not analysed further. *Examined in Layer 2: replaced by C-prim, C-asym, C-actual, C-partial, C-kind.* | C; §5 | examined |
| Ps-individ | Enough individuation to distinguish F from R and to take r, r′ as conditions of one relatum; no more. | R; §6 | examined |
| Ps-logic | The exposition uses identity, distinction, relation, and inference without attributing them to what it describes. | §1 | unexamined |

### Open questions

| Id | Question | § |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | What grounds the asymmetry of C in a given domain? | 5, 10 |
| Q2 | Can receptive dependence be explained in terms of more elementary relations? *Layer 2 leaves C unanalysed; the open branches B-power, B-ground, B-cause, B-reg are the candidate answers.* | 10 |
| Q5 | Does all aboutness rest on basic aboutness? Can aboutness by description, of the future, and of mathematical objects be built from registered contrasts? | 2, 10 |
| Q3 | Can registration of *which way* F is be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms, without admitting alternatives? | 7, 10 |
| Q4 | What order do acquisition and retention require, and is anything stronger than an asymmetric relation needed? | 9, 10 |

The reason is partly about content (an alternative must be held somewhere, which the core does not supply) and partly methodological (Mp-parsimony). Recorded under M4 as resting on both. | both | mario |
| Dec-restrictP | *Restrict P to basic aboutness.* P concerns basic aboutness, prior to concepts and descriptions: what is perceived or registered in any way. The draft's guard against differences supplied by a description is D-scope; the guard against the receiver belongs to C and C-asym. Whether two distinct contrasts can each hold partly in virtue of the other is left open, like transitivity. If it occurs, there are two instances of C and each contrast registers the other. | Content: the strict reading was grounded first in the definition of roles (Dec-asym), then in the route condition (Dec-asymscope). The first cold reader showed the second ground fails: a contrast made partly by its own registration is still borne by F, unlike a respect supplied by notation, so the route condition does not exclude it. And the first ground is not needed: roles are relative to an instance of C, and with mutual dependence there are simply two instances. Nothing else in Layer 1 uses the strict reading; R needs only that nothing holds in virtue of itself, which is kept, because without it every contrast would satisfy C with itself. Test-formal-dep had already shown that strict asymmetry does not exclude loops. Method: P does not require the strict reading, and a restriction that is neither required nor well grounded should not be carried (Mp-parsimony). | both | claude |
| Dec-claims | *Strength of the claims; what is ruled out and what is only not included.* After Test-cold-2. (1) That the registering is a difference is part of P2, a postulate, not a consequence. (2) P1 is argued up to two flagged steps. (3) "Registration" is only the defined term; the premise says every basic epistemic relation is a registration and does not claim the converse. (4) Of the former exclusions, only E2 is ruled out (resemblance and correspondence do not supply the dependence P2 requires); E1 is a matter of scope; E1-self says what is not a registration of anything in the target; E3, E4, E5 and E6 are read as "not among the conditions the premise requires", which does not show that registration can occur without them in a given domain. (5) A contrast has two positions. (6) "In virtue of" is bound by its conditions only as it figures in C. (7) Specification-independence is tagged once, as the condition of method. | Content: each point is a place where the paper claimed more than it had shown or tagged an item in two ways (Test-cold-2). Method: the aim is to claim nothing stronger than the support (Q0, "avoid overclaiming necessity"). Taken by Claude under the author's delegation of 2026-11-10; open to the author's critique. | both | claude |
| Dec-principles | *Two principles; actual terms argued; the necessity of an analysis.* The paper rests on two principles, determinacy and receptivity, from which P follows. That contrasts are between actual terms is a consequence, supported by three arguments about where alternatives might enter. The necessity claimed is that of an analysis: the conditions hold of every receptive relation to something in particular. The account says at which two points it can be refused. That the schema is met wherever one difference is due to another is stated as its main result, not as a defect: the base of the epistemic is not itself epistemic. | Content. (1) Calling P2 a postulate that no case can refute was wrong in the other direction from arguing it circularly: receptivity is what the relation under study is, and it has content, shown by what falls short of it. (2) "Actual terms only" was recorded as a decision resting partly on parsimony; it follows from receptivity, since only what holds can be that in virtue of which something holds, and each of the three places where alternatives might enter fails for a stated reason. (3) The same distinction between what dependence consists in and what is evidence of it resolves F-evidence and gives X-cf a ground that is not parsimony. (4) The permissiveness of the schema says something true: there is no primitive epistemic relation. | commitment | claude |

## Layer 2: ontology of the core

This layer examines the presuppositions of Layer 1, taking a position only where the core forces one.
It has no paper yet; § refers to the passage of Layer 1 it reads.

Layer 2 does not choose among analyses of the core's notions. It states what every analysis must
satisfy (the *trunk*) and keeps each compatible analysis open as a *branch*, following the rules
M1–M5 under **Method** above.

### The dependence in C: trunk

| Id | Kind | Statement | Requires | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-prim | Commitment | The dependence named by "in virtue of" in C is primitive. The core binds it by five stated conditions and does not analyse it further: it relates contrasts that both hold (C-actual); nothing holds in virtue of itself, and it has a direction (C-asym); it may be partial (C-partial); and whether it holds is fixed by no description of what it relates (C-local). It is of no one kind (C-kind). | C | 5 |
| C-kind | Commitment | *Kind-neutrality.* The core requires that C obtain, not that it be of one kind. What the dependence consists in (causal, constitutive, logical, or other) is fixed in each domain, if at all. | C-prim | 5 |
| C-local | Consequence | Whether C obtains in an instance is not fixed by descriptions of the relata, nor by what would obtain otherwise. Two instances alike in their relata and in their matching may therefore differ in whether C obtains: one is registration, the other mere correspondence (Figure 2b). | C, C-actual, E2 | 5 |

C-local leaves one question open: whether C in an instance can depend on *other actual instances*,
as in a pattern across cases. Reading A excludes alternatives, which are non-actual; other instances
are actual, so Reading A does not settle this. B-single and B-reg below answer it in opposite ways.

### The dependence in C: branches

| Id | Analysis | Adds | Compatible because | Closed if |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-single | *Singularity.* Whether C obtains is a fact about the instance alone. | Nothing beyond the instance; denies B-reg. | It requires no entity beyond the two contrasts. | Some later result needs C to be fixed by cases beyond the instance. |
| B-reg | *Regularity.* C obtains in an instance in virtue of a pattern across actual instances. | Other instances as a precondition of registration. | The instances are actual, so no alternative is admitted. | The pattern can be stated only over possible cases (E4), or fixes no direction (E2). |
| B-power | *Capacities.* C is the exercise of a receptive capacity of R, prompted by the contrast in F. | Capacities as constituents of relata. Settles Ps-modal: "admits" names a capacity. Explains C-partial: R's capacity is the remainder. | A capacity can be exercised in an actual instance. | A capacity can be identified only by what it would do in non-actual circumstances (E4, C-actual); or no sense can be given to capacities in non-physical domains (C-kind). |
| B-ground | *Constitution.* In some domains, the receiving contrast is partially grounded in the target contrast. | A domain-specific kind of C. | Ground relates facts, is asymmetric, holds between what actually obtains, and admits a partial form. | Ground requires the grounded to be nothing over and above its ground, against R being distinct from F; or its necessitation can be stated only over non-actual cases (C-actual). |
| B-cause | *Causation.* In physical domains, C is causal dependence. | A domain-specific kind of C. | Causation can be taken as asymmetric, actual and partial. | C is taken to consist in a transfer from F to R (E3). |

### The dependence in C: closed

| Id | Analysis | Contradicts | Closed by (M4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-cf | C holds because R would differ if F differed (counterfactual or interventionist dependence). | C-actual, E4: it requires non-actual cases. | Commitment; but Reading A, on which C-actual and E4 rest, was adopted partly on Mp-parsimony. |
| X-rule | C is a rule assigning conditions of R to terms of F. | Restricted to actual terms, a rule is only the pairing a with r, b with r′, which is matching (E2); anything more concerns values not taken (E4). | Commitment (E2); the second half also rests on Reading A. |
| X-transfer | C consists in something passing from F to R. | E3. | Commitment. |

Closed analyses are closed *as analyses of C*. As in Layer 1, the structures they describe may enter
later layers as further commitments.

### Decisions

| Id | Decision | Reasons | Basis (M4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dec-trunk | *Trunk and branches for C.* Keep the dependence in C primitive (C-prim) and characterize it by its properties, instead of choosing one analysis of it; keep every compatible analysis open as a branch. | The author's image: at the base of a tree we know the trunk, roots and branches, but not where the fruit is; a conflict may show only far along a branch. A primitive with stated properties is not a rival to the analyses but what they share, so keeping it primitive keeps the branches open. Claude had first recommended choosing generic dependence over capacities; the author asked why one must choose, and the answer is that one need not. | method |

### Proposals

| Id | Proposal | Open | By | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lead-repertoire | *Alternatives as actual conditions of the receiver.* Registration of which way F is may need no non-actual alternatives, if the alternatives are actual conditions of R. A receiver can have an actual, co-present differentiation into many conditions (as organon has a list of statuses); registering which way F is would be: which of R's actual conditions answers, through C, to the term realized in F. The other conditions are actual too, but nothing in F answers to them. | Whether this says which way F is, or only which way R is: the unoccupied conditions are actual in R, but their relevance to F seems to be exactly what alternatives supplied. If that relevance can be stated without modality, F-which closes within Reading A. | claude | proposed |
| Necessity | *Conditional, conceptual necessity.* The necessity the core claims is conceptual and conditional: necessarily, whatever is registered, of whatever kind, satisfies D, R and C, because this follows from what basic aboutness is (P, as restricted by Dec-restrictP). |  | claude | adopted |
| Which-position | *Which way as position in actual variety.* Registration of which way F is can be had from contrasts between actual terms, within a limit. R registers which way a term a of F is when the condition of R that answers to a through C is one of several actual conditions of R, each of which answers, through C, to some actual term of F, in this articulation or in another realized one. Which way a is, as registered, is which of F's actual terms a goes with: those whose condition it shares. The other conditions of R are relevant to F not as possibilities but because each answers to an actual term of F somewhere. |  | claude | proposed |
| Field-aspect | *Field as an aspect, not a domain.* Whatever is subject to differentiation is, insofar as it is, a field. Being differentiated is not a property of receivers: it belongs to the concept of field, which the core already has (D). So the clause "R admits differentiation of its own" can be stripped from R and reduced to F's concept: insofar as anything in R is differentiated, R is a field, for that reason and in that respect. What holds for the target in the author's original draft then holds for any field, the receiver included: the differentiation concerned is "attributable to its target, rather than one supplied entirely by an unrelated description" (epistemic_core.md, §1). Nothing follows about whether R and the target are the same field, parts of one, or given before one another. |  | mario | adopted |
| One-field | *One field; the receiver as a position in it.* There is one field: whatever is under consideration. Target and receiver are two parts of it, and which part is which is a matter of position in C, as Df-roles already says. The receiver does not distinguish anything: distinguishing is done by the account, for the receiver exactly as for the target (Df-specified). What the receiver needs is only that something definite in it holds partly because of the target's contrast; to be definite, that something must be a term of some articulation of the receiving part, which it admits as any part of the field does (D). |  | claude | withdrawn |
| Locus | *Modality and the locus of differentiation.* Given Reading A, the question whether differentiability is modal is the question where the differentiation is located: in the field, or in a subject who differentiates. What separates the two locations is the direction of "partly in virtue of", not modality. On the first, the receiving contrast K′ holds partly in virtue of the field's contrast K; on the second, K holds partly in virtue of K′. Both statements concern actual contrasts. A "can" appears only when a field is described apart from any registration, which the core does not do (D). |  | both | adopted |

### Objections

| Id | Objection | Attacks | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Obj-stroud | *Stroud's objection.* The core argues from P to its necessary conditions, which is the form of a transcendental argument. Stroud argued that such arguments establish at most what must be believed, or how things must seem, not how things are. Applied here: D, R and C might be necessary for registration *by receivers like us*, not "of any kind". | P | answered |
| Obj-harmony | *Agreement by arrangement.* Two contrasts might answer to one another exactly, with neither holding in virtue of the other, because both hold in virtue of a third. If that is a case of K′ being about K, P2 is false. | P | answered |
| Obj-intrinsic | *Dependence on what a term is in itself.* A receiver might depend directly on what a term a is in itself, with no contrast involved. Then the contrast K′ in the receiver and the contrast K between a and b would share a ground (a's character) without K′ holding in virtue of K, and C would fail of a case that looks like registration. | P, C | answered |

### Tests

The first result expected to separate the branches is Q3: whether registration of *which way* F is
can be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms. A branch that answers Q3 without
readmitting alternatives gains; one that can answer it only by readmitting them is closed by M2.

### Still to examine

Ps-modal (in part answered by B-power), Ps-relata, Ps-individ, Ps-logic.

### Literature

Records checked on 2026-10-23, texts not yet read for this layer: Anscombe, *Causality and
Determination* (1971), for singular causation (B-single, B-cause); Mumford and Anjum, *Getting Causes
from Powers* (2011), for B-power; Fine, "Guide to Ground" (2012), and Bennett, *Making Things Up*
(2017), for B-ground and for dependence as a generic notion with kinds (C-kind); Stroud,
"Transcendental Arguments" (1968), for Obj-stroud. Keys in `organon/library/refs.bib`.

## Frictions (all layers)

| Id | Friction | Kind | Between | Effect | Status | Resolution | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-readings | *Two readings of contrast.* The first draft could be read two ways: a contrast holds between co-present actual terms (Reading A), or between an actual term and its alternatives (Reading B). The arguments of the core went through on one reading and not the other. | ambiguity | Df-articulation | blocks | resolved | reject | Dec-readingA |
| F-time | *Time claimed necessary.* Draft-time claims more than P supports: P yields necessary conditions, and nothing in it requires time rather than some weaker order. | overreach | Draft-time, P | prompts | resolved | restrict | E5, Q4 |
| F-collapse | *Registration collapsing into matching.* With matching alone, registration cannot be told apart from resemblance or correspondence: the distinction the core needs disappears. | collapse | Df-matching, Df-registration | prompts | resolved | distinguish | C, E2 |
| F-cf | *Counterfactual analysis of C.* A counterfactual analysis of C requires non-actual cases; C-actual says C relates only contrasts that hold. | contradiction | X-cf, C-actual | prompts | resolved | reject | X-cf |
| F-ground | *Ground and distinct relata.* On standard accounts, what is grounded is nothing over and above its ground. R is distinct from F. B-ground can be kept only if partial ground between facts about distinct relata is coherent. | tension | B-ground, R | prompts | open |  |  |
| F-single | *Singularity or regularity.* Both branches are compatible with everything so far: nothing yet decides whether C in an instance is fixed by the instance alone or by a pattern across actual instances. | underdetermination | B-single, B-reg | prompts | open |  |  |
| F-which | *Which way F is.* Registration as defined is of a specified articulation. Later layers need registration of *which way* F is, and under Reading A this must be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms, without alternatives. Until it is, the epistemic apparatus cannot be built on the core (Q3). | gap | Df-registration, Dec-readingA | blocks | open |  |  |
| F-trivial | *Primitive dependence may be empty.* Characterized only as asymmetric, actual and partial, the primitive dependence may say too little: many relations have these properties. If no instance can be shown to differ from correspondence by C alone (and C-local says no description fixes it), C-prim risks being a name for the difference rather than an account of it. | triviality | C-prim | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-schema |
| F-descriptive | *Aboutness without dependence.* P covers any claim about X and requires that the distinguishing of X depend on X. Some aboutness seems to lack that dependence. A claim about whoever is the tallest spy is about that person whether or not anything in the claim depends on them: aboutness by description, as in Russell's theory of descriptions. Claims about future events, and on many views about mathematical objects, are about things that cannot act on whoever makes them (Benacerraf's problem for mathematical knowledge). If such claims are about their objects, P overreaches, and with it the claim that D, R and C are necessary for knowledge in general. | overreach | P | prompts | resolved | restrict | Dec-restrictP |
| F-subjectR | *The receiver made to distinguish.* The argument for R says that without a differentiation of its own, "nothing in R could distinguish registration from non-registration". Read literally, R does the distinguishing: something like noticing, which E6 excludes as a precondition of registration. Read as the account's distinguishing, the sentence says only that the theorist must be able to pick out something in R, which is a different and weaker claim. | ambiguity | Arg-R, E6 | prompts | resolved | reject | Dec-fieldaspect |
| F-pairing | *Term-by-term pairing not argued for.* Matching pairs each term of the target with its own condition of R: a with r, and b with r′. The argument for C needs less: one condition of R that holds partly because of the contrast between a and b, and something else in R for it to differ from. That other condition need not answer to b. Both pictures register the same thing, that a differs from b; the pairing adds structure that the argument for C neither uses nor justifies. | overreach | Df-matching, C | prompts | resolved | restrict | Dec-fieldaspect |
| F-groundD | *The ground of D stated too strongly.* The argument for D and exclusion E1 claim more than the ground of D supports. In the author's original draft, differentiability is admitted because the reconstruction "concerns a differentiation attributable to its target, rather than one supplied entirely by an unrelated description" (epistemic_core.md, §1): a condition of the route of explanation, not a thesis. The paper's argument for D turns it into an argument ("if every differentiation were supplied by the receiver, … what was registered would not be about F"), and E1 labels what is excluded "pure constructivism", which attaches the core to a position about a school of thought that nothing in the draft takes. | overreach | Arg-D, E1 | prompts | resolved | distinguish | Dec-groundD |
| F-respect | *"Contrast" names two things.* The text calls δ the contrast, "the respect in which the terms differ", and also calls K the contrast. But ⟨a,δ,b⟩ and ⟨c,δ,d⟩ share the respect δ and are two different contrasts. C, C-local and Which-position need the particular difference, not the respect. | ambiguity | Df-articulation, C | prompts | resolved | distinguish | Dec-repairs |
| F-rolesfield | *Roles defined on fields.* Df-roles made the target "the relatum whose contrast is depended upon". R allows one field to register its own contrast through a second contrast. Then target and receiver are the same field and the definition distinguishes nothing, although C-asym already holds "between contrasts, not between fields". | collapse | Df-roles, R | prompts | resolved | distinguish | Dec-repairs |
| F-specified | *The account's act inside the definition of registration.* C spoke of "the contrast of a specified articulation", and "specified" is defined as what the account does. Read literally, whether anything is registered depended on a theorist having specified it. The word is the author's draft's, where it reads as "particular"; the paper's definition of "specified" turned it into the account's act. | overreach | C, Df-registration, Df-specified, E6 | prompts | resolved | distinguish | Dec-repairs |
| F-indiscriminate | *Nothing singles out the registered contrast.* If K′ holds partly in virtue of K and partly in virtue of another contrast K*, it stands in C to both; if the dependence is transitive, also to whatever K depends on. Only the account's specification singled out which contrast "is" registered, and specification is not part of registration (F-specified). | gap | C, Df-registration, P | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-indiscriminate |
| F-Pterm | *P is about a term; the core delivers a difference.* P said that for X to be registered the distinguishing must depend on X, a term. The core registers "always a difference within F, never which way F is": a contrast in which X is one term. The argument for C passed from one to the other without comment. | tension | P, Df-registration, Arg-C | prompts | resolved | restrict | Dec-repairs |
| F-residues | *Residues of time and modality.* "Co-present" and "available together" have no stated meaning that is neither temporal nor spatial, against E5. "Distinguishable" in P is modal and "what it is not" is a negation, not an actual other term. "The manner in which R is receptive" reads as a disposition. "Differentiability" is a modal name for a claim decided not to be modal (Dec-groundD). | ambiguity | Df-conditions, P, C-partial, D, E5 | prompts | resolved | reject | Dec-repairs |
| F-partly | *"Partly" undefined, with an unargued remainder.* C-partial said the dependence is partial, with a remainder supplied by R. Nothing in P requires a remainder, and every argument of the core needs only "at least partly". The stronger claim also meets F-ground: if K′ held wholly in virtue of K, would it be a second contrast? | overreach | C-partial, C, F-ground | prompts | resolved | restrict | Dec-repairs |
| F-Dtrivial | *D true twice by definition.* A field is whatever bears a contrast (Df-field), and a realized articulation is one whose terms pick out positions of a contrast F bears (Df-realized). D follows from either definition alone. | triviality | D, Df-field, Df-realized | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-repairs |
| F-Punargued | *P carries the necessity and is not argued.* Registration is defined as an instance of C, so "whatever is registered satisfies C" is true by definition, and D and R follow from definitions. The informative claim of the paper is P: that what is perceived or registered in any way is a difference on which the registering depends. The paper starts from P and does not argue for it. Stroud's objection applies exactly there. | gap | P, Necessity, Obj-stroud | blocks | resolved | restrict | Dec-Pstatus |
| F-bears | *"Bears a contrast" has no stated properties.* The dependence in C is at least characterized (C-asym, C-actual, C-partial). "Bears a contrast" is characterized by nothing, yet it carries the whole difference between a contrast of the target and one supplied by a description. meta/Q-primitive (when is a primitive legitimate?) is open. | gap | Df-bears, D-scope, E1 | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-primitive |
| F-asymground | *Strict asymmetry grounded only in the definition of roles.* Dec-asym grounded "not even partly" in Df-roles: with mutual dependence neither role would be defined. | F-transorder | *Transitivity of dependence and the order of Layer 3.* If "in virtue of" is transitive and has no loops, dependence already orders contrasts, and is a candidate for the loose order Q4 asks for. Layer 1 leaves it open (Dec-asym); it cannot be decided apart from Q4. | underdetermination | C-asym, Q4, E5 | prompts | open |  |  |
| F-access | *The account's access to F is outside the account.* Specification picks out contrasts of F by description, and P, as restricted, does not cover aboutness by description. The theory uses a relation to its targets that it does not itself cover. | gap | Df-specified, D-scope, P, Dec-restrictP | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-repairs |
| F-P2circular | *The argument for P2 presupposed P2.* The argument rejected likeness because it makes K′ no more of K than of other contrasts, while registration by dependence is also indiscriminate; and it located what K′ is of in what accounts for K′, which is P2. | regress | Arg-P, P, Dec-indiscriminate | prompts | resolved | restrict | Dec-Pstatus |
| F-ubiquity | *On a liberal view of dependence every contrast is registered.* If constitutive dependence counts and collections are admitted, every contrast K is registered by the contrast between two collections that differ only in including its terms. The paper said an articulation may be realized while no contrast holds in virtue of it. | triviality | C-kind, Df-registration, Test-realizations | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-schema |
| F-sameness | *Registering that two terms do not differ.* That two terms are alike in a respect seems as basic as that they differ, and where there is no contrast there is nothing for C to relate. | gap | Df-registration, Dec-readingA, Q3 | prompts | resolved | accept | Dec-Pstatus |
| F-evidence | *Identifying the dependence may use what the core excludes.* In the causal case the dependence is identified by means that compare cases or consider what would happen otherwise. ### Withdrawn claims

| Id | Claim | Why withdrawn |
|---|---|---|
| K-contrast | *The registering is a contrast.* The registering is a contrast, not a single condition. For a registering to be some registering in particular it must be some way in particular (P1), and under Dec-readingA that is a position in an actual contrast. A receiver with one condition only, differing from nothing actual, would register nothing in particular. | 2026-11-10, by Dec-claims. It does not follow from P1, which concerns what a relation is of, not the registering. Its content is now part of P2 and is postulated. |

The core no longer excludes that a registered contrast holds partly in virtue of the contrast that registers it; it describes that as registration in both directions. |
| Draft-time | *Registration requires time.* Registration, or at least the acquisition and retention built on it, requires time. | Raised in the review of the first draft. The author objected that time is a loaded notion and that claiming it necessary overreaches: structures that are ordered but not temporal may suffice. The core keeps only an asymmetric relation, with transitivity left open (E5, Q4). See F-time. |
| One-field | *One field; the receiver as a position in it.* There is one field: whatever is under consideration. Target and receiver are two parts of it, and which part is which is a matter of position in C, as Df-roles already says. The receiver does not distinguish anything: distinguishing is done by the account, for the receiver exactly as for the target (Df-specified). What the receiver needs is only that something definite in it holds partly because of the target's contrast; to be definite, that something must be a term of some articulation of the receiving part, which it admits as any part of the field does (D). |  |
